item.title: Eastern North Pacific Tropical Weather Outlook
item.description:
000
ABPZ20 KNHC 291141
TWOEP

Tropical Weather Outlook
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL
500 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026

For the eastern and central North Pacific east of 180 longitude:

Active Systems:
The National Hurricane Center is issuing advisories on Tropical
Storm Karina, located well southwest of the southern tip of the Baja
California Peninsula, and on Tropical Storm Lowell, located well
east-southeast of the Hawaiian Islands.

Well Offshore of Southwestern Mexico:
An area of disturbed weather, associated with a tropical wave, is
located well to the south of southwestern Mexico. Environmental
conditions appear favorable for gradual development of this system,
and a tropical depression is likely to form in the next several of
days while it moves west-northwestward to northwestward at 10 to 15
mph.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...40 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...high...90 percent.

Central Pacific:
An area of low pressure could form well south or southwest of the
Hawaiian Islands in the next few days. Some gradual development is
possible thereafter and a tropical depression could form during the
middle part of next week while the system moves slowly
west-northwestward, well offshore of the Hawaiian Islands.
* Formation chance through 48 hours...low...near 0 percent.
* Formation chance through 7 days...medium...40 percent.

$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

Tropical Storm Karina Advisory Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
800 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026
 
...KARINA MAINTAINS INTENSITY AS IT MOVES NORTHWESTWARD OVER THE
PACIFIC OCEAN...
 
 
SUMMARY OF 800 AM PDT...1500 UTC...INFORMATION
----------------------------------------------
LOCATION...15.6N 117.6W
ABOUT 710 MI...1145 KM SW OF THE SOUTHERN TIP OF BAJA CALIFORNIA
MAXIMUM SUSTAINED WINDS...65 MPH...100 KM/H
PRESENT MOVEMENT...NW OR 310 DEGREES AT 12 MPH...19 KM/H
MINIMUM CENTRAL PRESSURE...989 MB...29.21 INCHES
 
 
WATCHES AND WARNINGS
--------------------
There are no coastal watches or warnings in effect.
 
 
DISCUSSION AND OUTLOOK
----------------------
At 800 AM PDT (1500 UTC), the center of Tropical Storm Karina was
located near latitude 15.6 North, longitude 117.6 West. Karina is
moving toward the northwest near 12 mph (19 km/h), followed by a
more westerly motion over the next day or two.
 
Maximum sustained winds are near 65 mph (100 km/h) with higher
gusts. Strengthening is forecast during the next several days.
Karina is forecast to become a hurricane over the weekend and could
become a major hurricane early next week.
 
Tropical-storm-force winds extend outward up to 230 miles (370 km)
from the center.
 
The estimated minimum central pressure is 989 mb (29.21 inches).
 
 
HAZARDS AFFECTING LAND
----------------------
SURF:  Swells generated by Karina will begin to affect portions of
the coast of southwest Mexico and the Baja California Peninsula
this weekend.  These swells are likely to cause life-threatening
surf and rip current conditions. Please consult products from your
local weather office.
 
 
NEXT ADVISORY
-------------
Next complete advisory at 200 PM PDT.
 
$$
Forecaster Katz/Beven

item.title: Tropical Storm Karina Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 800 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026 
000
WTPZ41 KNHC 291434
TCDEP1
 
Tropical Storm Karina Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP112026
800 AM PDT Sat Aug 29 2026

The current structure of Karina shows that the mid-level center is 
displaced from the low-level center based on some of the more 
recent microwave imagery. This is also reflected in the satellite 
imagery as well with the bulk of the convection displayed to the 
north. The most recent TAFB Dvorak intensity estimate is T3.5/55 kt 
and the objective intensity estimates from UW-CMISS are in the 
range of 45-58 kt. As such, the initial intensity has been held at 
55 kt. 
 
The storm continues on a northwestward heading of about 320/10 kt,
driven by a ridge of high pressure over the southwestern United
States. The storm is expected to slow down and turn westward as a
mid-level trough to the north weakens this ridge, allowing for the
ridge over the central North Pacific to build southeastward and take
over as the primary steering flow. The current NHC track is very 
similar to the previous track except for a few nudges, and it 
closely follows the HCCA guidance.

The SHIPS guidance maintains a favorable environment for the 
cyclone to intensify for the next 60 h. With light wind shear, 
warm sea-surface temperatures, and plenty of moisture in the 
environment, the conditions are conducive for Karina to continue 
to intensify. Reaching major hurricane status remains possible for 
Karina given the environmental conditions, however the cyclone will 
need to become vertically aligned first. After this weekend, SHIPS 
diagnostics indicate that the environment will gradually become 
less favorable, which will lead to a slow weakening trend. The 
current NHC intensity forecast is close to the middle of the 
guidance.

item.title: Tropical Storm Lowell Forecast Discussion Number 8
item.description:
Issued at 500 AM HST Sat Aug 29 2026 
330 
WTPZ42 KNHC 291438
TCDEP2
 
Tropical Storm Lowell Discussion Number   8
NWS National Hurricane Center Miami FL       EP122026
500 AM HST Sat Aug 29 2026

Lowell is slightly better organized than it was at this time 
yesterday, as the low-level center is now beneath the convective 
overcast. However, satellite imagery suggests that the mid-level 
center is still displaced west of the low-level center due to 
ongoing easterly shear. Overnight scatterometer data suggest that 
the maximum winds were 35-40 kt, so the initial intensity remains 
40 kt.

Lowell continues moving westward or 280/7 kt. A low- to mid-level 
ridge is forecast to strengthen north of the cyclone during the 
next couple of days, which should cause Lowell to continue westward 
with some a gradual increase in forward speed. This general 
westward motion is expected to continue through the weekend and 
into early next week. After that, the guidance becomes quite 
divergent in both direction and speed due to the potential effects 
of Tropical Storm Karina on Lowell's steering flow. By 120 h, the 
Google Deepmind Ensemble mean shows a continued westward motion, 
the GFS, UKMET, and the regional hurricane models show a slower 
motion toward the northwest, the ECMWF shows a slow motion toward 
the west, and the Canadian model turns the cyclone northeastward. 
The new track forecast lies between the Google Deepmind and the GFS 
cluster of models, and it is similar to the previous forecast.

The current easterly shear should continue for another 18-24 h 
before diminishing. The shear, along with mid- to upper-level dry 
air seen in water vapor imagery just north of the cyclone, should 
result in slow strengthening through 24 h.  After that conditions 
become more favorable, and the intensity forecast shows a faster 
rate of development. By the end of the forecast period, the 
intensity forecast becomes more uncertain due to Lowell's potential 
interaction with Karina. As noted before, a faster westward track
would likely keep the cyclones sufficiently separated and allow
Lowell to continue strengthening, while a slower solution could
expose Lowell to stronger shear associated with outflow from Karina.
The latest NHC intensity forecast has only minor tweaks from the 
previous forecast, and it lies near the middle of a guidance 
envelope that has a significant spread.
